name: Understanding and using numbers
description: Saying and understanding numbers, ages and quantities.

name: Understanding and using prices
description: Asking what things cost and stating prices.

name: Telling the time
description: Asking for and saying the time, and when things happen.

name: Asking for and giving directions
description: Asking where a place is and giving simple route directions.

name: Greetings and introductions
description: Greeting people and introducing yourself or someone else.

name: Giving personal information
description: Talking about your name, origin, home, family and job.

name: Describing habits and routines
description: Talking about what you usually or regularly do.

name: Connecting words: and, but, because
description: Joining simple ideas with and, but and because.

name: Verb to be (statements, questions, negatives)
description: Forms of be (am, is, are) in statements, questions and negatives.

name: Have got
description: Using have got for possession, mainly in British English.

name: Imperatives
description: Positive and negative commands and instructions (Sit down, Don't touch).

name: Question forms
description: Forming yes/no and wh- questions with do, does, did and be; word order in questions.

name: Present simple
description: Facts, habits and routines; third person -s; do/does in questions and negatives.

name: Present continuous
description: be + -ing for actions happening now or around now.

name: Past simple
description: Finished past actions; regular -ed and irregular forms; did in questions and negatives.

name: Past simple of to be
description: was and were in statements, questions and negatives.

name: Going to for plans and intentions
description: be going to + verb to talk about plans and intentions.

name: I'd like
description: Polite wanting with I'd like + noun or I'd like + to + verb.

name: Like, love, hate + -ing
description: Expressing likes and dislikes with verbs of preference followed by -ing.

name: Can and can't for ability
description: Using can and can't to talk about what someone is able to do.

name: Can and could for requests and permission
description: Asking for things, asking permission and offering help with can or could.

name: Countable and uncountable nouns; much and many
description: Countable vs uncountable nouns, how much vs how many, a piece of, a cup of.

name: There is / there are
description: Saying that something exists or is in a place.

name: Personal pronouns
description: Subject and object pronouns (I and me, they and them, it).

name: Possessive adjectives
description: my, your, his, her, its, our, their before a noun.

name: Possessive 's and s'
description: Showing possession with 's and s' (Mary's car, the students' room).

name: Possessive pronouns
description: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs used without a noun.

name: Common prepositions
description: Everyday prepositions such as at, to, from and with.

name: Prepositions of place
description: in, on, at, under, next to and similar words for location.

name: Prepositions of time: in, on, at
description: in, on and at with times, days, months and years; for and during.

name: Prepositional phrases of place, time and movement
description: Fixed phrases such as in the evening, along the beach, in the middle of the night.

name: Articles: a, an, the
description: Choosing between a/an and the for things mentioned for the first time or already known.

name: Determiners: some, any, a lot of
description: some, any and a lot of in positive sentences, negatives and questions.

name: Common adjectives and their position
description: Adjectives before a noun or after be; adjectives never take a plural -s.

name: This, that, these, those
description: Pointing to things near and far, in the singular and plural.

name: Comparative and superlative adjectives
description: -er or more + than, the -est or the most; irregular forms like good, better, best.

name: Adverbs of frequency
description: always, usually, often, never and where they go in the sentence.

name: Intensifiers: very, really
description: Making an adjective stronger with very or really.

name: Nationalities and countries
description: Names of countries and the matching nationality adjectives.

name: Personal information
description: Words for age, marital status, address and occupation.

name: Food and drink
description: Common foods, drinks, meals and containers.

name: Things in the town, shops and shopping
description: Places in town, types of shops and words used when buying things.

name: Travel and services
description: Transport, tickets, stations, airports and opening times.

name: Basic verbs
description: High-frequency verbs such as live, work, go, like and have.

name: Clothes
description: Items of clothing, materials and verbs like wear and put on.

name: Colours
description: Basic colour words and talking about favourite colours.

name: Size and dimensions
description: Words for size and shape such as big, small, long, high and wide.

name: Ways of travelling
description: Expressions like take the bus, go by train, fly and drive.

name: Family life
description: Family members, relationships and life at home.

name: Hobbies and pastimes
description: Free-time activities, sports and interests.

name: Holidays
description: Travel, accommodation and activities on holiday.

name: Work and jobs
description: Jobs, workplaces and everyday work tasks.

name: Shopping
description: Buying things, prices, sizes and returning items.

name: Leisure activities
description: Going out, entertainment and social activities.

name: Describing people
description: Describing someone's appearance and character.

name: Describing things
description: Describing an object by its shape, colour, size and material.

name: Making requests
description: Asking someone politely to do or give something.

name: Making suggestions
description: Suggesting plans with Let's, Shall we and Why don't we.

name: Giving advice
description: Telling someone what you think they should do.

name: Invitations
description: Inviting someone, and accepting or declining an invitation.

name: Offers
description: Offering help or something to someone (Can I help? Shall I carry it?).

name: Making arrangements to meet
description: Agreeing on when and where to meet and talking about fixed plans.

name: Expressing obligation and necessity
description: Saying what someone has to do or must do.

name: Describing places
description: Describing a town, building or region and what it is known for.

name: Describing past experiences and telling stories
description: Telling what happened in an event or story, in order.

name: Sequencing linkers: first, then, after that, finally
description: Ordering events in a story; later and subsequently at higher levels.

name: Wh- questions in the past
description: Questions with who, where, when, why and how about past events.

name: Past continuous
description: was/were + -ing for background actions and actions interrupted by another.

name: Used to
description: Past habits and states that are no longer true; didn't use to.

name: Present continuous for future arrangements
description: be + -ing for fixed future plans (I'm meeting him at 11).

name: Will vs going to
description: will for decisions made while speaking and promises; going to for plans already made.

name: Present perfect
description: have + past participle for experiences, recent events, for and since, ever, just, yet, already.

name: Gerunds
description: The -ing form used as a noun (Walking is the best exercise).

name: Verb + -ing or verb + to (like doing, want to do)
description: Choosing between -ing and to + verb after like, love, want and would like.

name: To + infinitive for purpose
description: Saying why someone does something (I went out to buy stamps).

name: Verb + to + infinitive
description: Verbs that are followed by to + verb, such as want, hope, forget and decide.

name: Zero and first conditional
description: If + present for general truths and real future possibilities with will.

name: Might and may for possibility
description: Saying something is possible but not certain.

name: Possibly, probably, perhaps
description: Adverbs of probability and where they go in the sentence.

name: Must and mustn't
description: Strong obligation and prohibition.

name: Have to
description: Obligation that comes from rules or circumstances.

name: Should for advice
description: should and shouldn't to give advice or say what is right.

name: Articles with countable and uncountable nouns
description: When to use a, the or no article with countable and uncountable nouns.

name: Determiners: all, none, enough, a few
description: A wider range of quantity words, including not any and (a) few.

name: Adjectives ending in -ed and -ing
description: bored vs boring, excited vs exciting: how you feel vs what causes it.

name: Adverbs of place, manner and time
description: Forming adverbs with -ly and using words like everywhere and tomorrow.

name: Adverbial phrases and word order
description: Where phrases of time, place and frequency go in the sentence.

name: Intensifiers: quite, so, a bit
description: Making adjectives stronger or weaker with quite, so and a bit.

name: Common phrasal verbs
description: Everyday verb + particle combinations such as get up, put on and take off.

name: Objects and rooms
description: Rooms in a house and the objects found in them.

name: Adjectives for personality, appearance and feelings
description: Words to describe what people are like, how they look and how they feel.

name: Education
description: School, university, subjects, exams and studying.

name: Describing feelings, emotions and attitudes
description: Saying how you or others feel about something and why.

name: Expressing opinions
description: Giving your view with phrases like I think, In my opinion, The way I see it.

name: Agreeing and disagreeing
description: Agreeing, and disagreeing politely or strongly.

name: Talking about films and books
description: Describing the plot and setting of a film or book and recommending it.

name: Starting and ending a conversation
description: Opening a conversation with someone and closing it politely.

name: Checking understanding
description: Checking that the listener follows you, or that you understood the speaker.

name: Interrupting, changing topic and resuming
description: Interrupting politely, moving to another subject and getting back to the point.

name: Linkers for cause, effect and contrast
description: however, therefore, on the other hand, nevertheless, consequently.

name: Markers in informal speech: right, well, anyway
description: Small words that organise casual conversation and show reactions.

name: Question tags
description: Tags like isn't it and didn't he to check or confirm information.

name: Would for past habits
description: would + verb for repeated actions in the past (not for past states).

name: Past perfect
description: had + past participle for an action before another past action.

name: Will and going to for predictions
description: going to for predictions based on evidence, will for opinions about the future.

name: Future continuous
description: will be + -ing for actions in progress at a future time.

name: Present perfect vs past simple
description: Choosing between a finished past time and a period up to now.

name: Present perfect continuous
description: have been + -ing for activities that started in the past and continue or just stopped.

name: Second and third conditional
description: Unreal present or future (if I won) and unreal past (if I had known).

name: Simple passive
description: be + past participle in present and past simple; using by for the agent.

name: Reported speech
description: Reporting what someone said or asked, with tense and pronoun changes.

name: Must and can't for deduction
description: Saying what you are sure is or isn't true based on evidence.

name: Must vs have to
description: Personal vs external obligation; mustn't vs don't have to.

name: Ought to
description: ought to for advice and what is the right thing to do.

name: Need to and needn't
description: Saying something is or isn't necessary.

name: Past modals: should have, might have, could have
description: Modal + have + past participle for regrets, criticism and past possibility.

name: Determiners: all the, most, both, several
description: A broad range of quantity words and how they combine with the and of.

name: Adjective + noun collocations
description: Natural adjective-noun pairs such as heavy rain, deep sleep, strong smell.

name: Adjectives vs adverbs
description: Choosing an adjective or an adverb (good vs well) and words with two forms (hard, direct).

name: Adverbs of degree and probability
description: extremely, too, probably, definitely and their position.

name: Comparative and superlative adverbs
description: more quickly, faster, the hardest, worse and the worst.

name: Intensifiers: too, so, enough
description: too + adjective, adjective + enough, so + adjective, and their word order.

name: Intensifiers: extremely, terribly, much too
description: A wider range of intensifying adverbs.

name: Separable phrasal verbs
description: Phrasal verbs whose object can go in the middle (turn it down) and less common ones.

name: Expressions for contrasting ideas
description: on the one hand, even though, mind you, nonetheless.

name: Collocations
description: Words that naturally go together, such as take a shower and a good chance.

name: Colloquial language
description: Informal everyday words and expressions used in casual speech.

name: Film
description: Types of film, people who make them and words to describe them.

name: Books and literature
description: Kinds of books, plot, characters and reading.

name: News, lifestyles and current affairs
description: Current events, society and the way people live.

name: Media
description: Press, TV, radio, the internet and social media.

name: Describing hopes and plans
description: Talking about intentions, wishes and future plans.

name: Giving precise information
description: Giving exact details such as places, dates, steps and specifications.

name: Expressing abstract ideas
description: Talking about ideas like freedom, poverty or education in general terms.

name: Expressing certainty, probability and doubt
description: Saying how sure you are that something is true or will happen.

name: Generalising and qualifying
description: Making general statements and limiting them (on the whole, provided that).

name: Summarising and evaluating information
description: Pulling information together and giving an overall judgement.

name: Speculating and hypothesising
description: Imagining possible causes and consequences (What if, Supposing).

name: Expressing reactions
description: Reacting with enthusiasm, disbelief or indifference.

name: Critiquing and reviewing
description: Evaluating a book, film, report or idea, with strengths and weaknesses.

name: Developing an argument
description: Building a case step by step with reasons, examples and a conclusion.

name: Taking the initiative in a discussion
description: Starting, steering and keeping a discussion or meeting on topic.

name: Encouraging others to continue or join in
description: Inviting someone to keep talking or to give their view.

name: Showing interest, sympathy and surprise
description: Reacting naturally while listening to someone's news or story.

name: Although, in spite of, despite
description: Linking contrasting ideas, including the structures after despite and in spite of.

name: Markers for formal speech and writing
description: furthermore, moreover, regarding, whereas, in conclusion.

name: Narrative tenses
description: Combining past simple, past continuous, past perfect and passive to tell a story.

name: Past perfect continuous
description: had been + -ing for an activity in progress before a past moment.

name: Future perfect
description: will have + past participle for something completed before a future time.

name: Future perfect continuous
description: will have been + -ing for duration up to a future point.

name: Mixed conditionals
description: Combining past condition with present result, or the reverse.

name: Wish and if only
description: Expressing wishes and regrets about the present and the past.

name: All passive forms
description: Passives in all tenses, with modals and in -ing and infinitive forms.

name: Relative clauses
description: who, which, that, whose; defining vs non-defining clauses and commas.

name: Can't have and needn't have
description: Past deduction (can't have been) and unnecessary past actions (needn't have).

name: Articles with abstract nouns
description: No article for general abstract ideas (happiness) vs the for specific ones.

name: Attitudinal adverbs
description: Sentence adverbs showing your attitude, such as frankly, clearly, apparently.

name: Intensifier collocations
description: Fixed pairs like totally exhausted, absolutely horrified, entirely satisfied.

name: Summarising expressions
description: in short, all in all, to sum up, in a word.

name: Arts
description: Painting, music, theatre, exhibitions and performances.

name: Expressing attitudes and feelings precisely
description: Describing mixed or strong feelings with precise, nuanced language.

name: Expressing opinions tentatively (hedging)
description: Softening your opinion (I assume, It could well be, I should think).

name: Expressing shades of opinion and certainty
description: Showing exactly how strongly you hold a view.

name: Conceding a point
description: Admitting the other side is partly right before making your point.

name: Emphasising a point
description: Stressing what matters most through phrasing, repetition and structure.

name: Defending a point of view persuasively
description: Arguing for an unpopular or difficult position convincingly.

name: Responding to counterarguments
description: Answering objections while keeping your own position.

name: Formal and informal register
description: Choosing words and phrasing that fit how formal the situation is.

name: Signposting informal speech and writing
description: mind you, on top of that, so, guess what.

name: Inversion after negative adverbials
description: Inverted word order after little, never, hardly and similar words.

name: False friends
description: English words that look like words in your language but mean something else (assist vs attend).

name: Idiomatic expressions
description: Fixed expressions whose meaning isn't literal, such as on the tip of my tongue.

name: Vague language and approximating
description: about, thirty-odd, sort of, or something like that.

name: Choosing precise vocabulary
description: Picking the most exact word for the meaning (upset vs devastated, shy vs antisocial).

name: Scientific development
description: Research, discoveries, technology and their effects.

name: Technical and legal language
description: Specialised terms used in technical documents, contracts and law.
